conservation_status.note_en: The global status is Least Concern; regional populations can still decline where grassland and burrowing prey are lost.
conservation_status.note_zh: 全球等级为无危；草地和穴居猎物丧失地区的地方种群仍可能下降。

description.en: The American badger is a low, powerful North American mustelid specialized for excavating burrowing prey. Long foreclaws, a wedge-shaped body and loose protective skin let it dig rapidly and defend itself underground or in open country.
description.zh: 美洲獾是北美洲低矮而强壮的鼬科动物，特化于挖掘穴居猎物。长前爪、楔形身体和松弛防护皮肤使其能快速掘土，并在地下或开阔地自卫。

anatomy.en: Adults commonly weigh about 6–12 kg and have a broad flattened body, short legs, long foreclaws, small ears and a white central facial stripe bordered by dark patches. Loose skin lets the animal twist when seized.
anatomy.zh: 成体通常重约6–12千克，身体宽扁，腿短，前爪长，耳小，面部中央有白纹并由深色斑块围绕。松弛皮肤使其被抓住时仍能转身。

ecology_and_behavior.en: Mostly solitary badgers locate rodents and other small animals by smell and hearing, then dig into burrows. They also eat reptiles, insects, eggs and carrion and may forage near coyotes when both predators make prey choose between surface and tunnel.
ecology_and_behavior.zh: 美洲獾主要独居，利用嗅觉和听觉定位啮齿动物等小动物，再挖入洞穴。它们也吃爬行动物、昆虫、卵和腐肉；有时与郊狼邻近觅食，使猎物必须在地面和洞道间选择。

habitat_and_distribution.en: The species occurs from southern Canada through much of the western and central United States into Mexico, favoring grassland, shrub-steppe, open farmland and soils that can be excavated.
habitat_and_distribution.zh: 该物种从加拿大南部分布，经美国西部和中部广大地区到墨西哥，偏好草地、灌丛草原、开阔农田以及可挖掘土壤。

range_review.comparison_en: The previous center, zoom and polygon coordinates are retained exactly. Authoritative text supports the broad distribution, but reusable authoritative boundary geometry was unavailable; the legacy polygon is labelled approximate, not verified.
range_review.comparison_zh: 原有中心点、缩放和多边形坐标完全保留。权威文字支持大致分布，但未获得可复用的权威边界几何；原多边形标为近似范围，而非已核实边界。

value.en: Burrowing mammals and other small prey
value.zh: 穴居哺乳动物及其他小型猎物

life_cycle_and_reproduction.en: Mating occurs in summer or early autumn, but implantation is delayed. Embryonic development resumes later so usually 1–5 cubs are born in a spring den; the mother nurses and protects them until dispersal.
life_cycle_and_reproduction.zh: 交配发生在夏季或初秋，但胚胎延迟着床。之后发育恢复，使通常1–5只幼崽在春季洞穴中出生；母獾哺乳并保护它们直至扩散。

detail.en: Strong shoulders and long claws move soil rapidly and open prey burrows.
detail.zh: 强壮肩部和长爪能迅速移土并打开猎物洞穴。

detail.en: A low broad form anchors the animal and moves through confined tunnels.
detail.zh: 低矮宽体可固定身体并穿过狭窄洞道。

detail.en: Timing embryonic development separates mating from spring birth when conditions are better.
detail.zh: 把胚胎发育时间与交配分开，使分娩落在条件较好的春季。

ecological_role.en: Badgers regulate burrowing rodents and their excavations aerate soil, mix nutrients and create holes later used by insects, reptiles and mammals.
ecological_role.zh: 美洲獾控制穴居啮齿动物，其挖掘会使土壤通气、混合养分，并形成后来被昆虫、爬行动物和哺乳动物利用的洞穴。

threats.en: Road mortality, poisoning campaigns aimed at prey, grassland conversion and trapping can reduce local populations even though the species remains widespread.
threats.zh: 道路死亡、针对猎物的毒杀、草地转化和捕捉会减少地方种群，尽管该物种仍广布。

actions.en: Retain open habitat and prey colonies, reduce indiscriminate poison use, provide road-crossing planning and monitor vulnerable peripheral populations.
actions.zh: 应保留开阔生境和猎物群落，减少无差别用毒，规划道路穿越措施并监测脆弱边缘种群。

key_features.en: Broad, very low mustelid with grizzled fur, a white stripe over the head, dark cheek patches and conspicuously long front claws.
key_features.zh: 宽而极低矮的鼬科动物，被毛灰杂，头顶有白纹，颊部深色，前爪明显很长。

similar_species.en: Striped skunks have a bushier tail and back stripes rather than the badger's flattened digging build. Wolverines are larger, darker and longer-legged.
similar_species.zh: 条纹臭鼬尾更蓬松，背部有条纹，没有獾的扁平挖掘体型。狼獾更大、更深色且腿更长。

communication_and_senses.en: Scent marks, hisses, growls, squeals and body posture warn rivals and predators; smell and hearing also locate hidden prey.
communication_and_senses.zh: 气味标记、嘶声、低吼、尖叫和身体姿势用于警告同类与捕食者；嗅觉和听觉也用于定位隐藏猎物。

seasonal_calendar.en: Activity declines in severe winter weather but true prolonged hibernation does not occur. Mating and delayed implantation produce spring births while prey activity changes seasonally.
seasonal_calendar.zh: 严寒天气中活动减少，但不会长期真正冬眠。交配与延迟着床使幼崽春季出生，猎物活动也随季节变化。

relationship_with_humans.en: Badgers can benefit farms by eating rodents but may dig in fields and embankments. They should never be cornered or handled; conflict prevention focuses on attractants and site-specific exclusion.
relationship_with_humans.zh: 美洲獾捕食啮齿动物可有利农田，但也会在田地和堤岸挖洞。绝不能逼近或触摸；冲突预防应管理诱因并按地点采取排除措施。

evolution.en: Taxidea taxus is the only living species of Taxidea, a North American branch of the mustelid family rather than a close member of the Eurasian Meles badger genus.
evolution.zh: 美洲獾是美洲獾属唯一现生种，属于鼬科的北美谱系，并非欧亚獾属的近成员。

field_signs.en: Large digging spoil piles, oval burrow openings and 5-toed tracks with long claw marks suggest a badger. Many mammals dig, so a clear track series or animal view is needed.
field_signs.zh: 大型掘土堆、椭圆洞口以及带长爪痕的5趾足迹提示美洲獾。许多哺乳动物都会挖洞，因此需要清晰连续足迹或动物影像。

text.en: Mating and birth are separated by delayed implantation.
text.zh: 交配与分娩通过延迟着床分隔。

text.en: A badger and coyote may forage near each other without forming a permanent team.
text.zh: 獾和郊狼可能在彼此附近觅食，但不会组成永久团队。

text.en: Loose skin helps a badger twist around inside a confined burrow.
text.zh: 松弛皮肤帮助美洲獾在狭窄洞穴中转身。

content.en: Powerful excavation serves hunting, shelter, birth and escape; soil type therefore shapes where the animal can obtain both prey and a secure den.
content.zh: 强力挖掘同时服务于捕猎、庇护、分娩和逃生，因此土壤类型会决定它能否同时获得猎物与安全洞穴。
